metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Plain versal initials, a few in ink but mostly in red which has sometimes oxidized to dark-red or even to near-black. No illumination. The selected frames include: added charms with Old English headings; Prudentius’ hymns, set to music through the contemporary addition of neums, and with elaborate interlinear and marginal glosses (primarily Latin); and the inscriptions, in Latin and Old English, recording the gift of the manuscript to Exeter Cathedral by Bishop Leofric (1050-72).

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Fly-leaves. Opening. Fol. iiv top half of page has fourteen elegiac lines on the Passio S. Romani; lower half has an Old English scribble in the margin, ‘scurfede hors’, next to a Latin account of Prudentius, his poems and their metres, beginning ‘[Au]rilius Prudentius Clemens iste’; both texts are in a hand perhaps a little later than the main manuscript.

Opening with interlinear and marginal glosses for Psychomachia. Fol. 109v has text starting with line 835: ‘Sed caua per solidum multoque forata dolatu’.
Fol. 110r has text starting with line 859: ‘Stagna lapis coibens ostro fulgebat aquoso’. One initial has not been filled in: '〈A〉t domus interior septem subnixa columpnis'. Page ends with line 883: ‘Nesciens marcenti florem submitteret colla’.

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Plain versal initials, a few in ink but mostly in red which has sometimes oxidized to dark-red or even to near-black. No illumination. The selected frames include: added charms with Old English headings; Prudentius’ hymns, set to music through the contemporary addition of neums, and with elaborate interlinear and marginal glosses (primarily Latin); and the inscriptions, in Latin and Old English, recording the gift of the manuscript to Exeter Cathedral by Bishop Leofric (1050-72).

metadata.value:
Opening with interlinear and marginal glosses. Fol. 110v has text starting with line 884: ‘Huius forma fuit sceptri gestamen Aaron’. Text of Psychomachia in this MS. breaks off at bottom of the page with line 908: ‘Spiritibus pugnant uariis lux atque tenebre’.
Fol. 111r has text of Hymn on SS. Emeritus and Celidonius: Peristephanon, Carmen I, Hymnus in honorem sanctorum martyrum Emeteri et Chelidoni calagurritanorum, start (no title). Large plain red initial ‘S(cripta sunt caelo duorum martirum uocabula)’. Page ends with line 23: ‘Vnicum deum fateri, sanguinis dispendio’. Interlinear and marginal glosses.
